It introduced a wide array of new techniques that profoundly influenced subsequent artists and helped explain its rapid and widespread impact. "una cosa que nos aportó muchísimo al Sardin Peppers y los Beatles fue una revolución técnica y un nuevo abanico de técnicas y grabación."

podcast.body: Issued on June 1, 1967, this album is considered the first proper Rock and Roll concept album. While it barely holds together conceptually, it is unified by a fictional band exploring life in post-war Britain, and its release opened the floodgates for other bands to create concept albums. "But the first proper Rock and Roll concept album was probably Sergeant Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club band, which was issued by the Beatles, of course, on June 1, 1967."

"en 1967 los Beatles publicaban el Sargent Péperes."

podcast.body: Released in July 1967, this album became the biggest pop phenomenon to date, marking the beginning of the "album era" and catalyzing the "Summer of Love" of 1967. Its immense success effectively overshadowed subsequent releases by The Beach Boys. "Sardines Peppers, de los Beatles, salió al mercado, y se convirtió en el fenómeno pop más grande hasta la fe."

podcast.body: Released on June 1, 1967, this album marked a significant shift in music, as it was explicitly designed to be listened to as a cohesive whole in one sitting, rather than just a collection of singles, opening up a "larger palette" for artists. "Then, on June 1, 1967, the Beatles released the Sargent Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band album. Yes, it featured a bunch of singles, but it was designed, explicitly designed, to be listened to as a whole and in one sitting."

podcast.body: Released on June 1, 1967, this album marked a significant shift in music, moving beyond "kiddie music" and the simple rock and roll sound. Its sophistication elevated music to an art form, contributing to the broader acceptance of rock as a serious genre. "The biggest change came on June 1, 1967, when the Beatles released Sergeant Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club band."

podcast.body: The Beatles did not bother to play Sgt. Pepper's live because they were already distanced from the stage and had no interest in returning. Instead, they focused on creating a truly creative, complex, and technically well-made studio work, even if it wasn't reproducible in live settings. "Se centraron más en intentar hacer un trabajo realmente creativo, realmente complejo y realmente bien técnicamente hecho, aunque eso no fuese reproducible en los escenarios."

podcast.body: The album marked its 50th anniversary, coinciding with its recognition as number one on Rolling Stone's list of the 500 greatest albums in history. It is considered a top contender across major rankings of best albums ever, opening up a new creative world for many artists and quickly becoming deeply rooted in popular culture. "se cumplían 50 años de su lanzamiento y está de número uno en la lista de los 500 mejores discos de la historia de los Rolling Stones."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Así se grabó el Sgt. Pepper's

podcast.body: The album represented a new phase of technically much more complex recordings for The Beatles, incorporating multi-track recording, overdubbing, and layered production processes previously developed by Brian Wilson for *Pet Sounds*. The band saw these advanced techniques as the future of recording. "con el Sargent Peppers entraban en una nueva fase de grabaciones técnicamente mucho más complejas."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Así se grabó el Sgt. Pepper's

podcast.body: The album's innovative seamless track transitions directly influenced the producer of Gloria Gaynor's 1975 album, *Never Can Say Goodbye*, which became the first album recorded in the "discomix" format. This format features interconnected tracks without gaps, where the music never stops and is harmonically linked. "un poco más adelante influenciado por Sardin Peppers en 1975 salía a que Neversa e Gudwai de Gloria Gainer, el primer disco grabado en formato discómics."

podcast.body: The final track from this album, "A Day in the Life," a masterpiece by John Lennon, received a lyrical reference in David Bowie's song "Young Americans." This connection was sung by Bowie's Luther Vandross-led chorus right in the middle of the song. "Boey drops a lyrical reference to the final track from the Beatles' Sergeant Pepper album, the John Lennon masterpiece, A Day in the Life."

podcast.body: This "legendary" album finally secured the Album of the Year Grammy for The Beatles in 1968, after they had lost twice to Frank Sinatra. Described as the Beatles' "bid for adult respectability," it was also seminal in the "shift of pop promotion from singles to albums" and seemed to bring the Grammys "somewhat up to date." "It figures that the Beatles bid for adult respectability, the legendary Sergeant Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club band, finally took album of the Year."

podcast.body: This album contains a notable curiosity: a recording of a dog whistle embedded in a locked groove at the end of the final track, "A Day in the Life". This unique feature, audible only to dogs, was known to cause them to react wildly and would play continuously without ending. "When a day in the life ended off the Sargent Pepper album in 1967, dogs went nuts."

podcast.body: This album was released on June 1, 1967, and was credited to Sergeant Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band, a pseudonym for The Beatles. For this record, The Beatles consciously assumed the role of this fake band, although they did not try very hard to conceal their true identity, making it "the world's worst secret" when it came to band pseudonyms. "But for that record, The Beatles assumed the role of this fake band."

podcast.body: A highly anticipated new remixed stereo version of "Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band," phonetically referred to as "sal y en otras partes," is scheduled for release on December 15th. This edition is significant due to long-standing controversy surrounding the Beatles' remasterizations and stereo versions, particularly "Sgt. Pepper's," which had one of the most debated "false stereo" mixes, leading to the mono version being more in demand. Extensive work has been done, remixing from the original analog recordings to create a quality stereo version, with hopes that this will be a less controversial or better-mastered stereo iteration. It will also be available on picture disc, though buying that format is deemed "a sin." "es la nueva versión del sal y en otras partes de los biters, remetclada la versión exterior del sal y en otras partes de los biters, porque es tan importante esta edición, pues porque siempre ha video mucha polémica sobre las remasterizaciones y las versiones en exterior de los biters y yo creo que el sal y en partes la versión en exterior es una de las versiones más polémicas de falso exterior que tenemos, en un de hecho mucha gente y sigue siendo mucho más demandada la versión mono que la versión exterior del sal y en partes, entonces es como que había que reacer y remetlar todo el sal y en partes para hacer lo exterior de nuevo, es ha hecho desde las grabaciones originales analógicas, se ha hecho un enorme trabajo para hacer una buena versión en exterior y parece que por fin vamos a tener una versión en exterior o una versión remasterizada menos polémica del sal y en partes, también va a salir en versión en pichordis, pero sinceramente comprarse esto en pichordis es un poco un pecado y ya está."
